help.title: How to read this map
help.months: Months refer to when police published an announcement. The events it describes may have happened earlier or at an unknown time.
help.hexagons: Hexagons show the number of selected announcements with a suitable location. One announcement counts at most once. A higher total does not establish a higher chance of crime.
help.places: Places shown nearby help you understand the surroundings. A nearby venue is not an incident location unless the announcement supports that connection.
help.routes: A displayed line may be a road or transport line mentioned in an announcement. It does not establish the exact journey or where on the line something happened.
help.unknown: An announcement stays available when its exact location or time cannot be confirmed. The map does not invent a point or date to fill the gap.
help.search: Search for names already included in this map. Some places have no recorded name, outline or type and will not appear in name searches.
help.language: Interface text is available in German, English and Chinese. Original announcements keep their source wording. Available translations are labelled as reading aids.
help.update: Police may correct or withdraw announcements after they are collected. The collection date shows when this dataset was saved, not when every event happened.
declaration.accuracy: A location may be approximate, incomplete or unknown. Read the announcement and its location note before interpreting a point, line or area.
declaration.timeliness: This is a collected dataset, not a live police feed. Delays, missing announcements and later source changes are possible.
declaration.statistics: These figures describe the selected announcements. They do not measure all crime, personal safety or the risk of visiting a place.
declaration.hateLead: “Possible hate crime” is an AI-assisted lead based on explicit signs of bias in the official wording. It is not a police finding. Identity, origin or neighbourhood alone are not evidence of motive.
declaration.affiliation: CrimeMaps is an independent project. Links identify the police or other organisations that published the sources.

analytics.title: Map visits
analytics.noData: Visitor statistics are not available yet.
analytics.note: Only page views you choose to share are counted; individual visitors are not counted. Groups below 20 views are hidden or combined. Totals are rounded down to the nearest 10, so displayed groups may not add up to the total. Checks limit abuse, but the figures can still be manipulated.

analytics.privacy: Counting is optional. Cloudflare estimates the country from the connection. CrimeMaps keeps country totals and temporary records used to limit repeated requests; these use a code derived from the connection address. CrimeMaps does not save your IP address. The browser check contacts Cloudflare, which processes connection data under its own terms.

methods.title: Statistics and how to read this map
methods.independent: CrimeMaps is an independent project. It is not a police website.
methods.officialSource: The map uses selected public police announcements. Each report links to its original source.
methods.munichSource: Munich uses records from POLIZEIKARTE, an independent project that links to police announcements. Its categories and reported dates are taken from that dataset.
methods.selection: Police announcements are a selected set of reports, not a list of every crime. One announcement may describe several events; follow-up announcements may describe the same event.
methods.geometry: A marked road, park or building can show the area mentioned in a report. It does not always identify the exact incident location. Unknown locations stay unknown. A nearby business is not evidence that an offence occurred there.
methods.tools: Software collects the sources and prepares the map. AI can assist with reading and classification; its suggestions need checking against the source.
methods.validation: Checks cover the source records, categories, location descriptions and map display in the included dataset. We have not measured a representative, model-specific accuracy rate for all 14 cities. Errors and missing information can remain.
methods.hate: A possible hate-motive label is an AI-assisted lead based on explicit bias evidence in the original report. It is not a police finding. Identity, nationality, religion and neighbourhood alone do not establish a motive.
methods.translation: Translations help readers understand the reports. The original wording and source link remain the reference; translations do not add address or time detail.
methods.updates: Collection and checking take time. The map may lag behind the source and miss reports. It is not a live warning service.
methods.noComparison: These statistics describe the included reports. They do not measure city safety, crime rates or hate-crime prevalence, and they cannot rank cities.
methods.statisticsUnavailable: Statistics are unavailable for this selection. The source and location limits above still apply.
methods.mapReferences: Reports included in the location totals: {count}. Reports without a usable location still appear in the announcement total.
methods.tagCoverage: Reports whose labels have all been reviewed: {complete}. Reports where the completeness of that review is unknown: {unknown}. An empty label list does not mean an event was absent.
methods.tagDenominator: Each label share uses all included reports as its denominator. It counts documented labels only. Missing labels and incomplete assessment can make the share smaller; this is not the prevalence of the event.
methods.dateUnknown: Reports without a single event date in the summary: {count}. Individual events may still have dates in the details.
methods.gapsKnown: The source coverage has known missing periods:
methods.gapsUnspecified: No complete list of missing periods is available. This does not establish complete coverage.

feedback.title: Private feedback
feedback.disabled: Private feedback is not connected yet. Sending is unavailable.
feedback.policy: Your message goes to the site operator and is not published. No name, email or account is required. Do not include victim identities, exact private addresses or allegations against individuals. This is not an emergency or police reporting service.
feedback.processing: Cloudflare handles the connection and checks for automated abuse. CrimeMaps does not save your IP address or a browser identifier. It briefly keeps a code derived from the connection address to limit repeated messages, so the service cannot promise full anonymity. Messages cannot be read after 30 days and are removed by the following daily cleanup. Cloudflare’s backups may keep deleted messages for up to seven more days on the Free plan.
feedback.consent: I have read the private feedback policy and will avoid personal details.
feedback.challengeNotice: This loads Cloudflare Turnstile. Cloudflare receives connection and browser details for its checks, and may use them to improve abuse detection. Send only after the check succeeds.
feedback.success: Your message was received privately. Keep the receipt number and secret deletion code. The code is shown only on this screen.
feedback.deleted: The deletion request was processed. To protect privacy, this response is also shown when the message is already deleted or cannot be found.
feedback.error: The message was not confirmed as received. Check the connection or try later.
feedback.rate: The feedback limit has been reached. Try later.
feedback.validation: Choose a feedback type, enter 10–2,000 characters and read the policy.
feedback.challengeFailed: The browser check failed or expired. Run it again.
feedback.retention: Only authorised site operators can read messages. Visitor comments are not published. You can delete a message with its receipt number and secret deletion code. No reply address is collected.

analytics.small: Too few page views to publish a total.
analytics.notCounted: This page view was not counted.
analytics.preference: Your browser’s privacy setting prevents this page view from being counted.
catalog.source-01.summary: Seven police-designated areas are listed. They are areas, not a list of businesses.
catalog.source-02.summary: Advice on preventing pickpocketing in crowded transport, shopping and event settings. It does not identify individual venues as crime hotspots.
catalog.source-03.summary: A study of night-time violence at two city-centre fast-food outlets. Its findings cannot be extended to the whole brand.
catalog.source-04.summary: Police work concerning night-time violence in the city centre.
catalog.source-05.summary: Police work on pickpocketing and snatch theft in the transport network.
catalog.source-06.summary: Pickpocketing advice for stations, platforms, escalators and boarding areas.
catalog.source-07.summary: Advice covers markets, transport, airports, attractions and hotel lobbies.
catalog.source-08.summary: Four designated nightlife areas are recorded in the checked source snapshot. It states an extension to 31 May 2027. This system differs from Berlin’s kbO areas.
catalog.source-09.summary: The 2025 area list includes a downloadable map. It concerns criminal influence on communities, not a visitor’s probability of becoming a victim.
catalog.source-10.summary: A 2021 source discusses prevention and enforcement at five main stations identified from police statistics. It is historical material.
catalog.source-11.summary: Advice on theft and damage in public car parks. It does not identify a particular car park as a crime hotspot.
catalog.source-12.summary: A 2022 reminder about pickpocketing at stations, on platforms and inside trains.
catalog.source-13.summary: Police work at stations and on railways during Easter 2023, with a specific reference to Napoli Centrale.
catalog.source-14.summary: Pickpocketing advice for events, restaurants, bars and transport connections.
rules.unlocated_announcement: Announcements without a precise map location
rules.reference_geometry: Outlines and routes help identify places. The exact event location may be unknown.
rules.circle_display: The 50 m circle is a display area, not a venue boundary.
rules.context_limitation: A reference to nearby places or a type of venue does not establish that an event occurred at this business.
rules.coverage_limitation: These announcements cover collected and reviewed public reports. They do not represent all crime in the city or personal risk.
rules.unknown_not_zero: An unknown location, or no suitable location for the totals, does not mean no crime occurred.
rules.possible_hate_lead: Possible hate crime is an AI lead based on explicit evidence of bias in the source, not a police finding.
rules.munich_upstream_exception: Munich uses POLIZEIKARTE’s categories and locations under the project’s agreed exception. The coverage still has gaps.
methods.munichValidation: For Munich, locations are checked against the city boundary and the map display is checked. Categories and dates remain those supplied by POLIZEIKARTE; the original narratives have not all been independently reassessed by this project.
methods.tagUnavailable: Label statistics are unavailable because complete assessment has not been established. Empty label lists do not establish the absence of an event.
basemap.vectorLanguageNote: Place names use the selected language when the map provides it; otherwise the original name is kept.
analytics.providerProcessing: Cloudflare checks connection and browser information, including your IP address, patterns from the encrypted connection and your browser identification. It uses this information to detect bots and improve its checks. Its privacy policy applies.
analytics.retention: Temporary request codes expire within two minutes and are normally removed from the application within three minutes. The service provider’s recovery backups may retain them for up to seven days. This processing is not fully anonymous.
project.initial: CrimeMaps is an open-source project at an early stage. Coverage is uneven, some locations remain unclear, and translations and ease of use still need work. Information may be missing or wrong.
project.contribute: If you’d like to help, raise a question, suggest a correction, or improve the code, wording or ease of use.
project.contributionPrivacy: Project discussions and code contributions are public. Leave out personal or sensitive information. For private feedback, use the option described on the page when it is available.
